definition: Apathetic means lacking interest, emotion, or concern.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word apathetic. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know apathetic should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The gym teacher could handle rowdy classes; what defeated him was an apathetic one — twenty students who would neither play nor protest.
A lukewarm response still holds a little warmth; apathetic means the warmth never arrives at all.
Uninterested is narrow and mild — one topic fails to attract you; apathetic is wider and heavier, a lack of feeling about things that ought to matter.
Numb goes even further than apathetic: the apathetic voter cannot be bothered to care, while a numb one has stopped feeling anything whatsoever, often from shock.

Listless is about missing energy rather than missing concern: a listless swimmer drags through laps she could normally fly through. Apathetic is about the concern itself — the feeling that should drive the effort never arrives. A listless person may care deeply and simply be drained; an apathetic one has nothing to summon.

Indifferent just reports no preference or concern about a particular thing, and it passes no judgment — a judge should be indifferent between the parties. Apathetic is the criticism: the capacity to care itself has drained away, across things that ought to matter, and the not-caring is the problem.

When the shop burned down, cards of sympathy filled the owner's mailbox for a week.
Apathetic means lacking interest, emotion, or concern.
The block association's founder papered every mailbox for the spring cleanup, offered free bagels, and moved the date twice for everyone's convenience.
The rest were not opposed and not busy — knock on any door and you met the same mild shrug.
The neighborhood was not hostile to the cleanup; it was apathetic.

Apathetic is stronger than uninterested and different from lazy: lazy people dodge effort, and uninterested people simply are not curious, but apathetic names a missing feeling — there is no spark of concern to act on in the first place.
Apathetic is a diagnosis, and usually a criticism: the capacity to care has gone missing.
Its cluster-mates carry different charges — indifferent just reports no preference or concern about a particular thing, and nonchalant describes a calm surface that may hide real feeling.
Call someone apathetic only when the not-caring itself is the problem.

When Dario took over the school paper, he expected the class election to be his biggest story of the fall.
Instead it nearly did not happen.
Only one student filed to run, and the sign-up sheet for the debate hung on the wall for two weeks with a single name on it.
"It's not that they're against anything," Dario told his advisor.
"You have to care to be against something." His editorial called the student body apathetic, and nobody wrote in to argue — which, he noted, rather proved the point.
The election went ahead with one candidate, one poster, and a turnout of eleven percent, most of whom admitted they had voted only because the lunch line passed the ballot table.
